piment: Chillies contain capsaicin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects at culinary doses.
amarante: Amaranth is a South American pseudo-cereal rich in complete protein, iron, and magnesium, and contains no gluten.
kamut: Kamut is an ancient durum wheat variety richer in protein and selenium than modern wheat, but contains gluten.
son d'avoine: Oat bran is the outer layer of the oat grain, very rich in beta-glucans that help lower cholesterol.
son de blé: Wheat bran is the husk of the wheat grain, highly concentrated in insoluble fiber useful for intestinal transit.
germe de blé: Wheat germ is the embryo of the wheat grain, rich in vitamin E, magnesium, zinc, and B vitamins.
mouton: Mutton and similar unprocessed meats provide complete protein, iron, and B vitamins, and are generally leaner.
brie: Brie cheese provides calcium, protein, and vitamin B12, but is fatty and salty.
sulfate de magnesium: Magnesium sulfate is an industrial laxative that can cause electrolyte disruption at high doses.
stearate de magnesium: Magnesium stearate is an industrial lubricating agent that may reduce nutrient absorption.
saumon d'elevage: Farmed salmon is raised intensively with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins; wild salmon is preferable.
huile d'olive: Olive oil is a basic culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and antioxidant polyphenols, benefiting cardiovascular health.
huile d'avocat: Avocado oil is a simple culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and vitamin E, stable for cooking due to its high smoke point.
vanille: Vanilla is a natural plant flavoring used in tiny amounts, with no additives or identified risks, distinct from synthetic vanillin.
ail: Garlic is a whole, unprocessed food containing sulfur compounds with antibacterial properties and beneficial effects on blood pressure.
sirop d'érable déshydraté: Dehydrated maple syrup retains natural antioxidants and minerals, serving as an unrefined natural sugar alternative.
sirop de mais: Corn syrup is an industrial syrup made from often-GMO corn linked to obesity, fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome.
gomme xanthane: Xanthan gum is a thickening agent that may disrupt digestion in sensitive people.
gomme guar: Guar gum is an industrial gelling agent that may cause bloating and digestive discomfort.
gomme konjac: Konjac gum is a thickener with a risk of intestinal blockage.
acide malique: Malic acid is industrially synthesized for food use and rarely extracted from fruit.
acide guanylique: Guanylic acid is an umami flavor enhancer metabolized into purines and not advised for people with gout.
guanylate disodique: Disodium guanylate is an umami enhancer in instant soups and snacks, not advised for people with gout due to purines.
guanylate dipotassique: Dipotassium guanylate (E628) is a potassium variant umami enhancer not advised for people with gout.
phosphate de diamidon hydroxypropyle e14: Phosphate de diamidon hydroxypropyle E1450 is an industrial starch derivative with a high glycemic index, impacting blood sugar levels.
caramel ammoniacal: Caramel ammoniacal is an ultra-processed caramel coloring made with ammonia, containing 4-MEI, a possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2B).
caramel sulfite caustique: Caramel sulfite caustique is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with sulfites, which may generate controversial by-products.
colorant caramel: Colorant caramel is an industrial caramel coloring often produced chemically, potentially containing carcinogenic 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B).
citrate de sodium: Citrate de sodium is an acidity-regulating salt made industrially, considered benign but indicative of ultra-processed foods.
extrait d'epices: Extrait d'epices is obtained by industrial solvent extraction, differing significantly from whole spices.
phosphate d'os: Phosphate d'os is extracted from industrial bones and may carry risks of heavy metal contamination such as lead and cadmium.
parabene: Parabene has been detected in breast tumors, raising health concerns.
guanylate de calcium: Calcium guanylate (E629) is a ribonucleotide flavor enhancer that boosts savory taste; not advised for people with gout due to purines.
ribonucleotides: Disodium ribonucleotides (E635) are a blend of E627 and E631 that enhance flavor and are often combined with MSG.
acide inosinique: Inosinic acid is an umami enhancer produced by bacterial fermentation that boosts MSG taste; not advised for people with gout due to purines.
inosinate dipotassique: Dipotassium inosinate (E632) is a potassium-based ribonucleotide flavor enhancer used in reduced-sodium recipes; not advised for people with gout.
inosinate de calcium: Calcium inosinate is a rare ribonucleotide umami enhancer; like others, it is not advised for people with gout due to purines.
ribonucléotides calciques: Calcium ribonucleotides are calcium salts of inosinic and guanylic acids used as umami enhancers combined with MSG; not advised for people with gout.
acide succinique: Succinic acid is an industrial acidifier with little long-term research on its effects.
citrate triammonique: Triammonium citrate is an industrial ammonium salt with limited toxicological data available.
zaatar: Zaatar benefits the body by providing natural herbs and spices rich in antioxidants and nutrients.
curry: Curry benefits the body by supplying curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory properties.
poivre rose: Poivre rose benefits the body as a mild, resinous dried berry with no additives.
sambal: Sambal benefits the body by offering fermented or crushed vegetables with natural flavors.
pâte de curry: Pâte de curry benefits the body by delivering fresh crushed plants rich in natural compounds.
pesto: Pesto benefits the body by combining whole foods like basil, pine nuts, and olive oil for nutrients.
humus maison: Humus maison benefits the body as a nutritious blend of cooked chickpeas and tahini providing protein and fiber.
reishi: Reishi benefits the body by providing beta-glucans from whole dried medicinal mushrooms.
roquefort: Roquefort cheese provides essential nutrients and protein, supporting muscle and bone health in small amounts.
cantal: Cantal cheese supplies calcium and protein, contributing to strong bones and muscle maintenance.
reblochon: Reblochon cheese offers fats and salt that provide energy and support cellular functions when consumed moderately.
crottin: Crottin goat cheese is lower in fat and easier to digest, benefiting those sensitive to cow milk.
gouda: Gouda cheese delivers protein and calcium, essential for bone strength and muscle repair.
noix du bresil: Brazil nuts and pure nut butters contain healthy fats, fiber, magnesium, and vitamin E, promoting heart health.
noix de muscade: Nutmeg is a spice used in small amounts that adds flavor without nutritional risk at culinary doses.
safran: Saffron is a natural plant-based coloring and flavoring that does not affect nutrition when used sparingly.
moringa: Moringa leaves provide concentrated protein, calcium, iron, and vitamin A, supporting overall nutritional health.
고추장: 고추장 is a Korean fermented chili paste made from chili, glutinous rice, and soybeans; some industrial versions add high-fructose syrup.
간장: 간장 is Korean brewed soy sauce traditionally fermented; brewed versions are preferable to chemically acid-hydrolyzed ones.
쌈장: 쌈장 is a Korean condiment blending doenjang and gochujang with a naturally fermented base.
nitrate de sodium: Nitrate de sodium is a preservative converting to nitrite and carcinogenic nitrosamines in the body (E-number not provided). Cured meats containing it are confirmed carcinogens (IARC Group 1).
ptfe: PTFE includes perfluorinated compounds (PFAS), nearly indestructible chemicals; PFOA is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1), PFOS possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B). Avoid exposure.
peg-: PEG- are ethoxylated ingredients that may contain traces of 1,4-dioxane, a possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2B). Their quality depends on purification; limit use.
sles: SLES is a cosmetic surfactant used for cleaning and foaming. It may cause skin and eye irritation and can be contaminated with carcinogenic 1,4-dioxane, so prolonged contact should be avoided.
parabenes: Parabenes are preservatives detected in breast tumors, raising concerns about their safety in cosmetics and foods.
paraben: Paraben is a preservative detected in breast tumors, raising concerns about its safety in cosmetics and foods.
parabens: Parabens are preservatives detected in breast tumors, raising concerns about their safety in cosmetics and foods.
butylparaben: Butylparaben is a preservative detected in breast tumors, raising concerns about its safety in cosmetics and foods.
PFAS / Polluants éternels: PFAS are chemicals found in grease-resistant food packaging; PFOA is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen since 2023. Prolonged contact should be avoided due to cancer risk.
pfas: PFAS are chemicals found in grease-resistant food packaging; PFOA is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen since 2023. Prolonged contact should be avoided due to cancer risk.
Parabènes (méthyl, éthyl, propyl, butyl): Parabens (methyl, ethyl, propyl, butyl) are cosmetic preservatives that disrupt hormones and mimic estrogen. They are suspected of breast cancer links and are known allergens, so prolonged contact should be avoided.
SLES (Sodium Laureth Sulfate): SLES (Sodium Laureth Sulfate) is a cosmetic surfactant possibly contaminated with carcinogenic 1,4-dioxane. It can irritate skin and eyes, so prolonged contact should be avoided.
